newsitem.title: JAPAN: Airbus Industrie defends its super jet plan.
newsitem.headline: Airbus Industrie defends its super jet plan.

text.p: Senior officials of Airbus Industrie on Tuesday firmly defended the planned development of a plane designed to hold up to 555 passengers and said it expects to launch the programme in December 1998.
"The A3XX will be the flagship of the 21st century," Airbus Industrie senior vice president John Leahy said at a news conference in Tokyo.

Airbus rival Boeing Co said in January that it has decided to halt plans to build its version of a superjumbo jet, saying its projected demand for fewer than 500 jets was not enough to generate profits.
But Leahy reiterated Airbus's own forecast of a market of about 1,400 planes seating more than 400 passengers over the next 20 years.
He said Airbus planned to launch the A3XX airliner programme in December 1998 and that the first aircraft would be in service in 2003.
Airbus was seeking partners, including Japanese companies, to bear 40 percent of the $8 billion development costs for the superjumbo plane, he said.
It would likely announce the signing of some memorandums of understanding with potential risk-sharing partners in the next few months, he added.
But Leahy declined to say which companies might join the venture.
Another Airbus official said a consortium of Korean companies, including Korean Air Lines Co, had recently expressed interest in the partnership.
Leahy said Airbus, a consortium of British, German, French and Spanish aerospace companies, expected to win more than half of the total global airliner market by around 2002.
"Shortly after the turn of the century we will pass the 50 percent market share point."
Leahy said he and other Airbus officials were in Japan for meetings with financial circles and leasing companies' officials. But he said they were not discussing financing of the A3XX programme.
